EPROM Field Retrofit Instructions
(Used in the Gauntlet’ Game)
A new set of erasable programmable read-only memory (EPROM) chips has been designed for your Gauntlet Game PCB to maximize game earnings. This new chip set modifies your game in several ways:

The mazes are changed to prevent expert plavers from. playing indefinitely. The new chip set changes the amount of food that can be found in the maze so that it is proportional to the number of players.

* The one-player game difficulty is increased, and to compensate, health per coin is also increased to help the beginner. ‘The manufacturer's recommended setting is now 700 health per coin instead of 600 health per coin.
° The Statistics screen is not bypassed if the Warrior Magic button is pressed too quickly.
* The Death character is unable to trap a player in an area from which he cannot escape. a

Setting the Game Options Perform the following procedure to set the game option settings:
1. Unlock the right coin door and locate the self-test switch on the Audio PCB.
2. Turn on the self-test switch.
3. Use the Warrior Magic button to advance the self-test to the Game Options screen.

4. Move the Warrior joystick down to move the red box to the Restore Factory Default Settings option. Move the joystick to the right or left to select es and exit from the Game Options screen by pressing the Warrior Magic button. This procedure clears the EEPROM of previous settings and replaces the manufacturer’s recommended default settings when the game enters the Attract Mode. Note: statistics and high score tables are automatically reset.
5. Turn off the self-test switch.
6. Refer to Game Options in the Self-Test chapter of the Gauntlet Operators Manual for further information.

Installing Your Chip Set Perform the following procedure to install the new chip set:
1. Turn the game power off.
2. After disconnecting all harness connectors, remove the Gauntlet Game PCB from the cabinet.

3. Locate each EPROM to be replaced, and remove it with a chip extractor tool. 4, For each new EPROM, align all of the pins on one side of the chip, and bend that row inward so that it is parallel to the other row.
